description:

**DJ Ewan, Europa Music**

For the Aftershow at The Albert Halls, DJ Ewan will be spinning a handpicked selection of classic tracks and crowd-pleasing favourites from his brilliant and extensive collection.

**DJ Nicola Meighan**

Nicola Meighan is an arts writer and broadcaster who has worked with the BBC, STV, The Herald and Mute Records over the years (touring with Moby, Goldfrapp, Depeche Mode, Erasure and Nick Cave), and has presented music and arts shows on BBC Radio Scotland for over a decade, interviewing guests like Dolly Parton, Martha Reeves, Patti Smith and Kylie Minogue. She hosts annual events including Stirling Pride and the Scottish Album of the Year Award, and regularly chairs author Q&As at Edinburgh International Book Festival, Aye Write, Granite Noir, Bloody Scotland and many more. She hosts The Saturday Social on Central FM, and Scottish Arts and Culture podcast A Kick Up The Arts. title: Ardal O'Hanlon
description:
Despite his best attempts over many decades to put the world to rights, it is still a colossal mess. And so, Ardal has no choice but to go out on the road again.

The Albert Halls - Seated

Date: Monday 14th September 2026

Door Times: 7.30pm

Tickets: £26.00 – £28.00

Oh, it’s all there! All the trademarks are in evidence in Ardal’s latest show. Beautifully crafted stand-up comedy? Yes. Celebrated use of language? Tick. Lateral thinking, surreal flourishes, sharp observations? Of course. As for the occasional profundity? Maybe.

Despite his best attempts over many decades to put the world to rights, it is still a colossal mess. And so, Ardal has no choice but to go out on the road again. Like the good comedy doctor he is, he fearlessly diagnoses the various pathologies and neuroses that are currently ravaging humanity. Disclaimer: No solutions provided. After an alarming experience at the supermarket, Ardal reflects on who he is as a man and a comedian. He examines his own ethnic and religious background. And thinks twice about the very core of his identity as a voice of reason. Is everything a big lie? With no major trauma of his own to draw on for material, apart from the drag of getting older, he also turns his gaze outwards at the joys and follies of contemporary life. Towel Animals? A.I.? Chair Yoga? Cauliflower as a main course? Yes. Yes. Yes. And Yes. No current idiocy is left unexamined. With a highly developed sense of the ridiculous, and proper comedy bones, NOT HIMSELF, is a testament to the healing power of humour. And the joy of jokes.

Ardal is not only an acclaimed stand-up comedian who has performed world-wide. He will be familiar to many from his appearances in TV shows such as TASKMASTER and WOULD I LIE TO YOU?, leading roles in DEATH IN PARADISE, FR TED, and MY HERO as well as cameos in DERRY GIRLS, THE WOMAN IN THE WALL, RETURN TO PARADISE and ROSIE MOLLOY GIVES UP EVERYTHING. He will soon be seen in the feature film, FRAN THE MAN, and the new Netflix series, HOW TO GET TO HEAVEN FROM BELFAST, as well as the CW drama, SHERLOCK AND DAUGHTER. Ardal is currently writing his third novel.

16+, u18s must be accompanied by an adult.

description:
Gary Meikle returns to the stage with another new show which has quickly become the yearly norm for him now.

Hi guys it’s me, Gary. These blurbs do my head in if I’m honest, each year I need to sit and write one out before I even know what stories I’m gonna share, well I mean I don’t have to write one I could pay something else to do it but f that they’d just write some mundane vague crap which I can clearly do myself. At least this way you know I’ve written it personally. So what’s the new show about? Again, I don’t yet, but it will contain at least one ‘yer maw’ Joke, what I do know is that it’ll be another brand new 80-90 minutes of stories, opinions and observations about me, and my family as well as you all its always about people and the mad shit we do, sometimes animals but more often than not it’s about people and the stupid scenarios we end up in. I wonder if that’s now enough wordage to cover the minimum blurb requirement? I guess we’ll see, and I’ll see you all soon maybe – oh, one last thing, my show isn’t suitable for small people, some of it might be about them, in fact it definitely will but, yeah they ain’t getting in 🙂

Expect a set that includes tracks from the outstanding Long Road Out Of Eden album. The Eagles’ music is timeless, appealing to audiences of every age, bringing back memories and touching the hearts and souls of each new generation.

Grab your ticket for an unmissable hour in the company of two of Scotland’s finest crime writers.

It is 30 years since crime fiction’s most infamous mantlepiece featured in Chris Brookmyre’s debut novel Quite Ugly One Morning. Now, three decades later his irrepressible investigative journalist Jack Parlabane returns in the ingenious Quite Ugly One Evening. Abir Mukherjee follows his award-winning bestseller Hunted with the equally action-packed and thought-provoking thriller The Pinnacle which sees murder strike on the 65th floor of Mumbai’s grandest luxury skyscraper.

Nadine Mathieson’s barnstorming debut The Jigsaw Man established her as the creator of deliciously dark novels, and she continues to delight with the gory new thriller The Shadow Carver. title: In Conversation: Val McDermid and Denise Mina
description:
Join two of the biggest names in Scottish crime fiction for an extra special final event to wrap up Bloody Scotland 2026. Between them, they have published more than 60 novels, been translated into more than 40 languages and have sales in the multi-millions. Val’s latest novel (co-written with Jo Sharp) is This Door of the Seas. Part of the acclaimed Darkland Tales series, it is an epistolary historical novel about the late 17th-century Darien Venture – Scotland’s ill-fated attempt to establish a trading colony in the jungles of Central America. Denise’s latest novel is The Good Liar, a standalone thriller in which blood spatter expert Claudia O’Shiel finds herself with a critical choice to make that might put her life on the line.

This event will be chaired by the literary agent Jenny Brown.

title: John Lydon - I Could be Wrong, I Could be Right
description:
He’s a legend and an icon, a revolutionary and an immortal. John Lydon – aka Johnny Rotten – changed the face of music and sparked a cultural revolution. The frontman and lyricist of the Sex Pistols and Public Image Ltd (PiL) caused a political earthquake and transformed music for good. To coincide with the publication of his new book, the brilliant, funny and insightful I Could Be Wrong, I Could Be Right, he is touring the UK. Lydon will talk about how he sees life, along with his unique and extraordinary career, and take audience questions during a pyrotechnic, one-off tour. Lydon will be sharing his thoughts with audiences. He Could Be Wrong. He Could Be Right.

VIP and meet’n’greet packages are available. Signed copies of the book will be available.

title: Richard Osman with Mark Billingham
description:
When Richard Osman last appeared at Bloody Scotland in 2019, he was an unpublished author best known for presenting Pointless and House of Games. Fast forward seven years and things have changed remarkably. title: Russell Watson - An Intimate Evening with 'The Voice'
description: Get ready for an unforgettable night with one of the world’s most captivating performers. Russell Watson – the original crossover superstar – exploded onto the music scene with The Voice, a debut album that shattered records and won hearts across the globe. Since then, he’s sold millions of albums, performed for royalty, presidents and popes, and shared the stage with musical legends. Now, in his most intimate tour to date, Russell takes you on a journey through the highs and lows of an extraordinary life – from chart-topping success to surviving not one, but two life-threatening illnesses. With warmth, humour, and a voice that soars, he’ll share the personal stories behind the spotlight. Expect powerful renditions of beloved classics, spine-tingling vocals, and behind-the-scenes tales from a man who’s truly lived it all. This is more than a concert – it’s a rare chance to spend an evening up close with The Voice himself.

title: Stirling Mini Melodies
description:
Looking for a joyful Friday morning activity for you and your little one? 🎶👶 Join Stirling Mini Melodies, a warm and welcoming weekly music group for babies, toddlers, and their parents and carers. Through songs, movement, sensory play and simple instruments, little ones can explore rhythm and melody while building confidence, coordination and early communication skills – all while having lots of fun! Expect a relaxed, inclusive atmosphere where grown-ups are encouraged to join in too, creating special moments through shared musical experiences. And because we know parents deserve a treat, free tea and coffee will be available after each session – the perfect chance to unwind and meet other local families.

  • Sensory-rich musical play
  • Singing, movement and instruments
  • Parent and carer participation encouraged
  • Free tea and coffee after class
  • Free to attend!
Classes run Fri 21 Aug – Fri 9 Oct, 10:30am–11:30am 📍 Lesser Hall, The Albert Halls Please note sessions on 18 & 25 Sept will take place in the Attic at Tolbooth (upstairs with lift access). FREE | Booking required Suitable for babies and toddlers with their parent or carer. One adult booking covers up to two infants (please let us know how many children will be attending when booking). 👉 Music plays a vital role in early years development, supporting language, physical coordination and emotional wellbeing – so come along, sing, play and make new connections with other families. Find out more and book your place at StirlingEvents.org, or get in touch with our Box Office. 🎵💛
address: The Albert Halls, Dumbarton Road, Stirling, FK8 2QL

title: Tide Lines
description: Tide Lines are a band whose story stretches from the wild expanses of the Scottish Highlands to the beating heart of Glasgow. In June 2025, they celebrated a landmark moment with their fourth album Glasgow Love Story via their own Tide Lines Music label, which landed at No.1 in Scotland and No.11 in the UK Official Album Charts — their highest UK chart position to date and third Scottish No.1. Across three earlier albums — from the sweeping romanticism of Dreams We Never Lost through to 2023’s An Ocean Full of Islands (which charted at No.13 in the UK and No.1 in Scotland) — Tide Lines built a reputation for expansive, anthemic songs and magnetic live performances. 2024 was a milestone year: three euphoric nights at Glasgow’s legendary Barrowland Ballroom, 14 summer festival appearances across the UK, a sold-out European run through the Netherlands, Denmark and Germany. They closed the year with a 14,000-ticket Scottish tour that included a triumphant return to the Usher Hall. Now, as they mark 10 years together, the story continues with the recently released Glasgow Love Story, an album rooted not in island remoteness but in the pulse of the city they now call home. Robertson describes it as “a love letter to Glasgow. It’s the city we started the band in, and it’s been a constant presence in our journey ever since.” He continues: “We’ll always be influenced by where we’re from. The Highlands gave us our first songs, but Glasgow gave us a stage and an audience. Both places are written into what we do.” The record paints a panoramic portrait of the city: the sandstone tenements glowing red in the evening sun, rain-slicked streets shining under lamplight, and the everyday lives unfolding in its bars, dancehalls and quiet corners. With special guest Calum Bowie Tickets: £37 (incl £2 bf) Standing 14yrs+ Balcony 5yrs+ Under 16yrs must be accompanied by an adult
